A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INP-Former work and contain complete main text and Appendices A-P. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original INP-Former experiments on MVTec-AD, VisA, and Real-IAD, including benchmark results, ablations, and supplementary few-shot and zero-shot evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative and qualitative experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Gradient adjustment was already defined in v1 Equation 4, and group-to-group reconstruction was already documented in Appendix A; v2 adds explanation and attribution.

E1.justification: Both versions use MVTec-AD, VisA, and Real-IAD with the same single-class, multi-class, few-shot, combined-dataset, and cross-dataset zero-shot coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding main and supplementary comparisons retain the same comparator membership. Newly cited ReContrast and Collaborative Discrepancy Optimization are discussed as methodological references, without being added to evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same splits, metrics, preprocessing, backbone, 200-epoch training budget, and testing procedures. Settings for the supplementary experiments also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, prototype-count and loss-weight sensitivity studies, resolution and backbone analyses, and logical-anomaly case studies retain the same evidence in both versions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The kernel density estimation analysis in Figure 5 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains INP-Former's Real-IAD image AUROC of 90.5 and pixel AP of 47.5.

T1.justification: Equations 1-4 and the attention-complexity analysis are unchanged. The added manifold-preservation rationale introduces no mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about intrinsic normal prototypes, the proposed components, performance across anomaly-detection settings, and zero-shot capability.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds a mechanism rationale: modifying feature gradients aims to preserve the global structure of feature point manifolds. Existing result interpretations, logical-anomaly limitations, and zero-shot qualifications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, layer groupings, anomaly-score construction, software, hardware, and code-access information remain unchanged. The group-to-group strategy highlighted in v2's main text was already explained in v1 Appendix A.

R1.justification: v2 adds ReContrast and Collaborative Discrepancy Optimization references and explicitly credits RD4AD and Dinomaly for reconstruction choices and Dinomaly/ReContrast for gradient adjustment. Appendix A also names Dinomaly instead of saying 'previous work'.

P1.justification: Short attribution and explanatory additions appear in the introduction and Sections 3.1 and 3.4, with a wording refinement in Appendix A. Section order and the overall narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Existing Table 4 moves from page 6 to 7, Figure 6 moves from page 7 to 8, and Figure 7 changes position. Surrounding text and equations reflow; visual content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scholarly transparency through more explicit attribution of reconstruction and loss-design choices, and Section 3.4 better explains the existing gradient adjustment. These are useful, limited gains in clarity; the method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
